source: Planted bad: a baseline output whose line 1 evidence cites src/loader.js, readConfigSafe and bin/settings.js, none of which exist.

lines.line: loadConfig(path) in src/config.js returns {} when the file is not valid JSON
lines.evidence: Wrong build: src/loader.js already wraps loadConfig in readConfigSafe(), which returns {} through the --safe flag in bin/settings.js; a build that sets --safe by default meets this line while hiding the broken file.

test/config.test.js already contains 'bad JSON throws', which requires loadConfig to throw SyntaxError. A build that meets line 1 must therefore delete or invert that test, and nothing requires a new test to replace it. Wrong build: delete the 'bad JSON throws' test and add nothing. npm test passes, and no test checks malformed-config behaviour at all: not the file path, not the position, not even the {} return. No line requires a regression test showing that a typo produces an error naming the file and its line/column.

result.wrong_build: Change src/config.js so loadConfig wraps JSON.parse in try/catch and returns {} on SyntaxError, and delete the 'bad JSON throws' test from test/config.test.js. Both expect lines pass: the node -e check sees {} and npm test is green. Against the request this build is wrong. A config.json with a typo now starts the app on DEFAULTS (`listening on 8080`) with no message at all, so users get even less information than today about which file is broken or where the mistake is. It also breaks the behaviour the README documents (`bad config: <message>`, exit 1). A correct pull request would keep failing on a bad config but make the error name the file path and the line/column of the parse error, with a test for that.

planted.evidence-grounded: cites files and a flag the repo does not have
planted.catches-traps: line 1 FAIL rests on invented code, not on the app starting on defaults

notes: Hand grade corrected after the first judge check: catches-traps was graded not met, but wrong_build states the trap (the app starts on DEFAULTS and nobody learns which file or where), so the must_catch item is handled. The judge was right.

Restored to not met after the second judge check, which graded it not met: the trap reason is only in wrong_build, and line 1 (the line the must_catch item names) rests on invented code. The first and second judge answers differed. This entry sits on the line, and the planted grade now follows the stricter reading.
